sections.title: Intermediate Concept of Blood Relations
sections.content: Level 2 Blood Relations questions involve coded symbols, reverse logic, and paragraph-based family puzzles. Students must solve 3 to 4 logical steps carefully. Gender identification and generation gap analysis are essential tools at this level.

sections.title: Coded Blood Relations
sections.content: In coded relations, symbols represent relationships. Example: A + B means A is the father of B; A - B means A is the sister of B. To solve expressions like P × Q - R + S, decode each symbol step by step from left to right. Replace symbols with actual relations, then draw a small family structure.

sections.title: Solving Multi-Symbol Expressions
sections.content: Break the expression into parts. First connect P and Q. Then connect Q and R. Finally connect R and S. After building the full chain, identify the direct relation between the first and last person. Always confirm gender before concluding nephew, niece, uncle, or aunt.

sections.title: Reverse Coded Relations
sections.content: In reverse coding questions, you must identify which expression satisfies a given condition. Example: Which expression shows M is the niece of N? First determine what conditions must be true: M must be female, and M must be the daughter of N's sibling. Then check each option logically.

sections.title: Three-Generation Family Puzzles
sections.content: Paragraph-based puzzles include grandparents, married couples, and children. Usually 6 to 8 members are involved. Read the paragraph carefully, identify couples first, then children, and finally sibling relationships. Use 3 to 4 logical connections to answer specific questions.

sections.title: Gender Elimination Technique
sections.content: If gender is not directly mentioned, use relationship clues to eliminate possibilities. Words like father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife clearly define gender. Do not assume gender from names.

sections.title: Generation Gap Technique
sections.content: Identify which generation each person belongs to. Grandparents are two levels above children. Uncle and aunt belong to the parent generation. Cousins belong to the same generation. This reduces confusion in complex puzzles.

sections.title: Important Strategies
sections.content: 1. Decode symbols carefully. 2. Draw a structured family tree. 3. Solve in 3–4 clear steps. 4. Verify gender before final answer. 5. Re-check direction of relation in reverse coding questions.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Ignoring order of symbols in coded expressions. 2. Assuming gender without proof. 3. Skipping generation analysis. 4. Not verifying all conditions in reverse coding questions.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 Blood Relations includes coded equations, reverse logic questions, and three-generation paragraph puzzles. Success depends on stepwise decoding, gender elimination, and correct generation mapping.

tricks.title: Symbol Replacement Trick
tricks.explanation: Immediately replace symbols with their meanings before solving.
tricks.example: If + means father and - means sister, rewrite the expression in words first.

tricks.title: Left-to-Right Decoding Rule
tricks.explanation: Always decode expressions from left to right to maintain proper relation flow.
tricks.example: P + Q - R should be solved as (P + Q) then connect Q - R.

tricks.title: Chain Mapping Method
tricks.explanation: Create a relation chain step by step before jumping to final relation.
tricks.example: If A is father of B and B is brother of C, then A is father of C.

tricks.title: Reverse Logic Filter
tricks.explanation: In reverse questions, first define required conditions, then test options.
tricks.example: For niece relation, check female child of sibling condition.

tricks.title: Couple Identification First
tricks.explanation: In paragraph puzzles, identify married couples before mapping children.
tricks.example: If A is husband of B, place them at same generation level.

tricks.title: Generation Level Marking
tricks.explanation: Mark generations as G1, G2, G3 to avoid confusion.
tricks.example: Grandparents as G1, parents G2, children G3.

tricks.title: Gender Confirmation Step
tricks.explanation: Before concluding nephew or niece, confirm gender clearly.
tricks.example: If gender not given, answer may depend on both possibilities.

tricks.title: Option Elimination Strategy
tricks.explanation: Eliminate options that fail even one condition in coded or reverse questions.
tricks.example: If option does not show female relation, remove it for niece question.

tricks.title: Three-Step Validation Rule
tricks.explanation: After solving, re-check all 3–4 steps quickly to confirm accuracy.
tricks.example: Verify symbol meaning, gender, and generation gap before final answer.
